text:
alex_cheng: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak on private VPCs we're seeing a perf regression on smaller nodes for long convo workloads. p95 jumped and KV-cache hit rate dropped. Posting quick profile & config ideas, please chime in.

maya_garcia: ugh — can you paste the p50/p95 numbers and sequence distribution?

alex_cheng: quick summary from canary region (A10-ish, 32GB):
- baseline (before patch): p50=120ms, p95=280ms for seq<=256; p95=420ms for seq>512
- after kernel change: p50 ~130ms, p95=560ms for seq>512, tail spikes at ~1.2s on some requests
- KV-cache hit rate: dropped from 96% -> 82% for long chats (seq>1024)
- observed more small-batch kernel fallbacks and increased GPU memcpy stalls

jordan_wong: any flamegraphs or traces? sounds like batching got worse for long prefix hits.

alex_cheng: attaching snippets (pasted):
```
Flame: hot path shows extra memcpy + kernel-select loop
CPU: kernel_selector() called 3x per request for large seq
GPU: memcpy wait ~8-12ms spikes per token window
KV: cache eviction count increased by ~30% during tail
```

samir_patel: theory: kernel-selection heuristic now prefers a faster per-token kernel that behaves worse when KV hits cause irregular seq lengths. If batch formation mixes short+long it can blow up effective batch token budget. We should split queues by seq_len buckets and enforce token_budget targets per-batch.

devon_ops: agree. For private/VPC we need per-vpc overrides because hardware constrained. We already support per_vpc config — here's a suggested override you can push as a quick mitigation:
```yaml
per_vpc_overrides:
  <vpc-id>:
    batch:
      max_batch_tokens: 2048
      token_budget_target: 1024
      max_queue_ms: 30
      seq_len_buckets: [128, 512, 1024]
      kernel_fallback_threshold: 0.7  # fallback to stable kernel if confidence < 0.7
      prefer_small_kernels_for_seq_gt: 512
```

maya_garcia: I like the seq buckets. Also consider a priority queue rule: if token_budget_consumed_by_head >= 0.8 of target, force immediate flush to avoid starving short requests.

jordan_wong: +1. Also add a metric for kernel_selector.invocations_per_request and selector.hysteresis_score. Current selector has no hysteresis so tiny noise flips kernel choices often. That causes repeated warmups.

samir_patel: alternative quick fix: lower kernel_fallback_threshold to 0.6 and reduce max_queue_ms to 20ms for private small-GPU pools. That reduces batching depth and memory pressure at cost of some throughput.

alex_cheng: rolled the per_vpc override to canary cluster (vpc-03f). Test results after 45m:
- p95 for seq>512: 310ms (was 560ms)
- KV-cache hit rate: 92% (up from 82%)
- cost delta: +5% token-cost due to less aggressive batching / smaller kernels

devon_ops: good trade for customer SLAs. We should add this overrideable knob to the private console with a one-click rollback. CLI snippet to set: `rcli vpc set-config vpc-03f --batch-config ./override.yaml`

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Applied per_vpc override to vpc-03f in canary (release-2026.03.17). :rocket:

alex_cheng: follow-ups:
- samir: add hysteresis & selector telemetry (priority)
- jordan: add seq-bucketed queue + immediate-flush rule
- devon: expose per-vpc toggle in console + cli
- maya: own canary validation and perf dashboards for these knobs

samir_patel: note on kernel selection logic: current estimator uses rough FLOP heuristic that underestimates memory-bound kernels. I'll add a GPU-memory-bound flag and make selection cost model include memcpy stall penalty.

jordan_wong: also let's add a regression test in perf CI: synthetic traffic with mixed short/long sessions to catch this behaviour before kernel-level rollouts.

alex_cheng: thanks everyone — keeping the canary running for 24h before wider rollout. Will post final numbers. :thumbsup:
